Interaction experiment: EACH particle's lab kinetic energy ~ N(0.6, 0.4) eV truncated at 0.012 eV, drawn independently, so the pair carries a net momentum and the centre of mass moves; K_CM below is the invariant derived from the two, and each trajectory is integrated in that COM frame.  (b_y,b_z) ~ N_2(0, sigma^2 I), hence b ~ Rayleigh(sigma = 500 pm), truncated by rejection at R_match/2; both dipoles isotropic.

Interaction trajectories: 200/200

Explicit outcome-censoring model:
  physical outcome observed / administratively censored / numerical failure = 200 / 0 / 0
  P(physical classification | K_CM,b): constant rate 1 (200/200); covariate effects not estimable
  P(numerical failure | K_CM,b): constant rate 0 (0/200); covariate effects not estimable
  IPCW positivity: min fitted completion probability=1, max clipped weight=1 (floor 0.05), effective N=200
  IPCW assumption: physical classification is missing at random conditional on sampled (K_CM,b); NumericalFailure is modeled separately and is not called a physical event.

Interaction outcome summary (200 trajectories):
  Collision              1  (0.5%)
  Scattering           179  (89.5%)
  Para-Positronium       6  (3.0%)
  Ortho-Positronium     14  (7.0%)
  bound total           20; para:ortho = 6:14 (isotropic expectation 1:3)
Para = parallel magnetic moments (antiparallel spins, S=0); ortho = antiparallel moments (S=1).
IPCW physical-class distribution under MAR(K_CM,b) (Hajek normalized):
  Collision              0.5%
  Scattering            89.5%
  Para-Positronium         3%
  Ortho-Positronium        7%
This is a censoring-sensitivity estimate, not a replacement for the raw counts above.

Sampled beam parameters:
  all trajectories   <K_CM> = 0.704281 eV,  <b> = 637.357 pm

Quasi-closed orbit of the captured pairs (20 of 20 bound events):
  T  minimum 0.151816 fs
  T  mean    28.0038 fs
  T  maximum 540.46 fs
  revolutions observed: minimum 0.000370055, mean 0.949993, maximum 1.32494
T is the Kepler period of the osculating capture orbit, the longer of its capture-time and window-close values.
The revolution count is what the bound observation window actually covered, NOT a count to collapse: these pairs are
followed only long enough to classify them, so the window is bounded by boundObservationTimeCap.

Bound-state CREM collapse time (14 of 20 bound events):
  minimum 0.00119982 ps
  mean    3.86777 ps
  maximum 12.2475 ps
This is the extrapolated classical inspiral time to the pair's inner boundary (the Compton barrier for e+e-,
the collision boundary for every other pair) from the orbit-averaged radiated power (secular
dE/dt=P model; experiments 1 and 2 now measure this mechanically instead, so the two are NOT comparable).  It is not a quantum
annihilation lifetime.  Only bound events whose observation window closed a full Kepler orbit are included:
below that the window samples the post-periapsis leg, whose instantaneous power is not an orbit average.
  6 of 20 bound events were excluded by that gate (window shorter than one orbit).
Bookkeeping identity residual (not a conservation test): median 2.33592e-05; independent |dE_LL-vs-flux|/E_rad median 1.00109.
